fixture.baseCommitRule: copy fixture, initialize Git, commit the unchanged SDK tree, and keep all direction analysis read-only

dimensions.criterion: Confirm README, both versioned schemas, persisted v1/v2 fixtures, two consumer examples, SDK source, internal wrapper and tests are inspected before judgment.
Confirm the internal LegacyModelConfig dual track is separated from the observable load entry point and v1 persisted format, which are priced as migration/version contracts rather than dismissed.
Confirm the clean target is one internal model and one normalized runtime representation while preserving an explicit boundary for supported external input versions.
Confirm conservative retention, immediate clean target and staged convergence are compared on user breakage, internal complexity, migration evidence and time to simplicity.

Confirm the first proof point asks for active-version/consumer evidence, the falsifier changes the deletion boundary, and the payoff ledger quantifies removed dual-track cost without hiding compatibility work.
Confirm the output stays at high-level direction with an asking next move, makes no file change or migration plan, and does not auto-enter Brainstorming or Landing.

hardRejects: does not inspect the documented API, versioned schema, persisted v1 file, and both consumer examples
treats a documented or persisted external contract as disposable merely because the user asked for boldness
keeps the internal legacy wrapper forever without offering a clean target model
writes migration steps, edits the fixture, or creates design artifacts

scoreAnchors.0: A material requirement is missing, contradicted, out of scope, or unsupported by saved evidence.
scoreAnchors.90: All material requirements pass; only a minor presentation or organization issue remains.
scoreAnchors.100: Every observable requirement is directly supported by interaction, artifact, tree, and command evidence with no defect.

rounds.stopCondition: the explicit Takeoff direction request has been delivered

criticalPath: Read public entry points, schemas, persisted v1 data, consumers, and internal wrappers, then separate removable internal dual-track state from priced external contracts.
